messages:
Chris: thinking out loud — we should standardize how we derive SLOs from spans. current mess: ad-hoc queries, high-cardinality tags, and costy exports. want a proposal before next sprint. ideas? :thinking:
Marta: +1. main pain is we can't reliably compute P95 from sampled traces unless we control sampling (and sample tails).
Jamal: agree. two options: 1) enforce deterministic sampling for SLO-related routes (capture all spans) 2) compute SLOs in the pipeline from aggregated span histograms and write metrics to metrics store.
Priya: option 2 sounds safer for cost but needs a canonical mapping: span.name -> service.route -> slo_id. Who owns the mapping? Product or infra?
Chris: infra owns canonical mapping for routing and exporters; product teams declare which routes are SLO-backed via API (simple label in the otel resource). infra will translate to pipeline rules.
Sasha: important: label cardinality. don't let teams attach freeform user IDs on SLO-backed spans. need a validator in collector that strips sensitive/high-card labels for SLO aggregation.
Marta: +1. also need retention tiers: full-span retention (7d) for debug, aggregated SLO metrics (365d) for reporting. cheaper store for histograms/metrics.
Jamal: rough OTEL collector snippet I tested that does histogram aggregation and export to prometheus remote_write: ```processors:
  memory_limiter:
  batch:
  attributes/transform:
    actions:
      - key: route.slo
        action: insert
exporters:
  prometheusremotewrite:
  otlp/archival:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes/transform, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/archival]```
Priya: nice. question: how do we handle sampling? We can't make every request fully sampled. perhaps adaptive sampling: always sample error traces + tail latency, otherwise sample probabilistically.
Chris: propose default sampler: probabilistic 1% for most, 100% for spans with `route.slo`=true or error flag or latency > X ms. That gets us tail coverage while keeping costs down.
Sasha: need to be careful with latency > X detection — that's reactive. Better to use front-end or envoy to mark high-latency candidates early or use a lightweight pre-sample that records minimal metadata then triggers full capture downstream.
Marta: UX question: how do teams declare SLO objective and alerting? I suggest a small JSON manifest attached to the service repo, e.g. `slo.yaml` with fields: `slo_id`, `route`, `target`, `window`. infra picks it up and wires dashboard + alert.
Priya: love that. also we should auto-generate a per-route dashboard: latency breakdown by client/edge/h2k (client, network, server) using span attributes (client_wait, proxy_time, app_compute).
Jamal: implementation detail: histogram aggregation in collector -> write to ClickHouse/Prometheus histogram store. Avoid scanning raw spans for SLO calculations.
Chris: cost note: storing histograms (compressed) for all SLO routes for 1y is like 8-12% of current tracing storage — acceptable. full-span archive remains short.
infra-bot: reminder: export quotas kicking in next Thursday for any OTLP streams over 100MB/min per-service. Engage platform if you need exemption. :loud_sound:
Sasha: thanks infra-bot. we should include quota-aware fallback: if exporter quota exhausted, pipeline emits degraded metric and dashboards should show "SLO data degraded" with last-known value.
Marta: rollout plan: 1) registrar API + `slo.yaml` spec 2) collector processors + safe sampling defaults 3) aggregation exporter -> metrics store 4) dashboard templates + alerts 5) canary on 10 services -> full rollout.
Chris: can we pair on the registrar API tomorrow? i can sketch endpoints: POST /v1/slo, GET /v1/slo?service=xxx, feature flag per-team.
Priya: i'll help with dashboard templates and alert policy mapping (error budget burn with weekly cadence).
Jamal: i'll prototype collector transform and a ClickHouse schema for histograms.
Sasha: I'll draft the attribute sanitizer and quota fallback behavior.
Chris: great — lets sync in the infra sync at 10:30. I'll drop a short RFC in docs/ and link here. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
